case_evidence.description: Frozen Python W3 workflows/_dense_regression.py: requires explicit source config with empty preprocessing plan, complete common-grid TrajectorySet, declared source parameters, a real timed fit step, explicit analyst/derived decisions and no silent model selection or processing.

Sixteen complete multichannel trajectories observed at 15 times with named source curve IDs. FPCA 1/2 integer components and .85 proportion, unscaled/dimension_sd; FOS HC1 ordinary least squares with declared single predictor under independent curve or equal-weight repeated-curve participant units, both channels or a selected channel, participant predictors constant within unit.

Actual native FPCA fitted means, quadrature-weighted covariance eigenspectrum, retained eigenvalues and explained variance ratio, signed-score Gram invariant, genuine measured fit step, source FPCA provenance, exact source report, score and four-column variance tables. Pinned Python tests cover component counts 1/2 and variance proportion .85, scaling none and dimension_sd.

Strict source mode requires a valid scalar boolean and exactly declared complete-grid configuration, source-compatible integer or fraction count, permitted scaling, named predictors and unit metadata. Rejects nonempty preprocessing, malformed predictors, unsupported model units and inconsistent participant grouping; arbitrary Python exception types are not reproduced.

Nine exact ordered W3 source-scientific workflow result fields, complete source config including empty preprocessing, true source-named elapsed fit step, analyst/derived decision values and criteria, original workflow provenance, exact reporting prose and source-schema tidy scientific tables. Nested R model classes remain scientific S3 analogues.

FPCA: declared quadrature-weighted dense common-grid principal components without hidden preprocessing, retaining specified components/variance or scaling. FOS: pointwise multichannel Gaussian functional OLS with HC1 errors across independent curve/participant means and no smoothing or mixed-effects substitution.
